To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The polymerization of benzene and methane in a glow discharge leads to the formation of a polymeric material that shows some similarities with the material formed in an electron beam.
the polymerization of organic molecules in an electric discharge is a complex process and that the resulting polymers have a structure that is not yet fully understood.
The structure of the polymer film depends on the type of discharge, and the polymer structure changes after irradiation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of polymerization processes in glow discharges and with the electron-microscopic investigation of the products of these polymerizations.
the study of the structure and properties of the polymer films formed by the action of an electric discharge in benzene and methane.
the study of the structure of the polymers formed during glow discharges of benzene, methane and other hydrocarbons.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the electron microscopically observed structures in the polymerized films are the result of the chemical structure and the physical conditions of the polymerization process.

the structure of a polymeric material is a function of the chemical composition of the monomer, of the reaction conditions, and of the time of polymerisation, and that the structure of the polymeric material in turn is a function of its history of mechanical deformation.
the structure of the polymer is determined to a great extent by the chemical nature of the starting material.

the structure of the carbonaceous polymer films formed in benzol or methane glow discharges is very similar to the carbonaceous polymer film structure produced by electron bombardment.
the structure of polymerized carbonaceous films is determined by the nature of the polymerization process, i. e. by the chemical composition of the polymerizing gas and by the temperature.
